### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.misc

### Neovim version

0.10.x

### Description

The [autocmd setup by `setup_auto_root()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.misc/blob/645fb9367c19bb485902e54e5451425981498601/lua/mini/misc.lua#L214) executes on `BufEnter`, so directory change occurs after a file is opened in the project. This is conflicting since if I run `MiniFiles.open()` or run `pwd` in the cmdline while in starter screen, it returns the nested directory within.

The issue is more apparent while using plugins like folke's [persistence.nvim](https://github.com/folke/persistence.nvim). On the starter screen, I have binded the `s` key to run `persistence.load()` but since the autocmd hasn't run yet, it fails to detect the root and thus cannot open the saved session.

Conversely, [vim-rooter](https://github.com/airblade/vim-rooter) changes the directory as soon as neovim is opened (on `VimEnter` event I believe) so the issue isn't there.

Using:
NVIM v0.10.3
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1736781742

persistence.nvim as session manager
alpha-nvim as starter

PS: Just shifted to using more modules of `mini.nvim`, appreciate the work! Do let me know if I should add more details for better understanding.


### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    MiniDeps.add('echasnovski/mini.nvim')
    MiniDeps.add('folke/persistence.nvim')

   MiniMisc.setup()
   MiniMisc.setup_auto_root()
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Save a session by opening a bunch of windows/buffers and exit.
5. Navigate to a nested path, try to run `persistence.load()` inside while on start menu.

Note: after reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

Unfortunately, I don't understand the issue and reproduction steps (step 5 in particular).

Immediately after opening Neovim the current directory is the one from which `nvim` command is executed (i.e. the current directory of the terminal emulator). This is expected.

When any kind of dashboard is opened during startup, it shouldn't have a meaningful path-like buffer name, so auto-root is not applied. So the current directory should still be the same as of the terminal emulator.

Would you mind elaborating on the use case, please?

> Unfortunately, I don't understand the issue and reproduction steps (step 5 in particular).

If the root path is `/home/user/repo/`, navigate inside a nested directory like `/home/user/repo/assets/images`. After entering the dashboard or starter the cwd is the same as terminal cwd, not the project root (since the autocmd hasn't run yet).

> Immediately after opening Neovim the current directory is the one from which nvim command is executed (i.e. the current directory of the terminal emulator). This is expected.
Would you mind elaborating on the use case, please?

I understand, but `persistence` would try and fail load the session for the cwd. If I am working on the project `/home/user/repo/` and enter neovim at `/home/user/repo/assets/images`, running `persistence.load()` won't work since the cwd is still inside the images directory. Similarly, `mini.files` would also list files under the cwd only.

This is in contrast to other rooter plugins like `vim-rooter`, where the cwd is changed to the project root as soon as neovim is opened.

> If the root path is `/home/user/repo/`, navigate inside a nested directory like `/home/user/repo/assets/images`. After entering the dashboard or starter the cwd is the same as terminal cwd, not the project root (since the autocmd hasn't run yet).

I see, thanks for clarifying. Yes, this is an intended behavior. If user started Neovim from not project root, then it is assumed that there was a reason behind it and auto-rooting should not affect that. It only takes effect for currently opened *file from the project*.

On Neovim>=0.10 setting up forced auto-root during startup is pretty straightforward:

```lua
local adjust_cwd = function()
  local root = vim.fs.root(vim.fn.getcwd(), { '.git', 'Makefile' })
  if root ~= nil then vim.fn.chdir(root) end
end
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('VimEnter', { once = true, callback = adjust_cwd })
```

Make sure to put this code somewhere where it is not lazy loaded (i.e. it should be executed during startup).

Closing as working as expected.

title: [mini.misc] `setup_auto_root()` executed on `BufEnter`
